breakfast.name: Bakes (Fried Dough)
instructions: Mix dough, rest 10 min
Flatten pieces
Deep fry until golden
breakfast.description: Puffy fried dough — Caribbean morning staple.

breakfast.name: Cocoa Tea with Bread
instructions: Grate cocoa stick into boiling water
Add milk, sugar, spices
Simmer 5 min, strain
Serve with buttered bread
breakfast.description: Rich cocoa drink from local cocoa sticks.

breakfast.name: Saltfish Souse
instructions: Boil salt cod 5 min, drain, flake into pieces
Mix with sliced onion, cucumber, Scotch bonnet
Dress generously with lime juice and olive oil
Add parsley, black pepper
Let marinate 10 min
Serve with sliced avocado and bakes (fried dough)
breakfast.description: Salt cod 'souse' — cured fish dressed with lime, onion, and fiery Scotch bonnet. A bright, acidic morning dish that wakes you up faster than coffee.

lunch.name: Mountain Chicken (Crapaud)
ingredients: 4 crapaud (giant dodo frog) legs — or substitute chicken thighs if crapaud is unavailable
Seasoning: lime juice, garlic, thyme, scallion, parsley, Scotch bonnet pepper
Creole sauce: tomato, onion, garlic, thyme, Scotch bonnet, lime
instructions: Clean frog legs, season heavily with lime, garlic, thyme, scallion, Scotch bonnet
Marinate overnight in the fridge
Dredge in seasoned flour
Fry in hot oil until golden and crispy — the meat inside should be white and tender
Make Creole sauce: sauté onion, garlic, add tomato, thyme, Scotch bonnet, lime
Serve fried legs with Creole sauce
Note: crapaud is now endangered — this dish is increasingly made with chicken as a cultural preservation
lunch.description: Dominica's national dish — not poultry, but the legs of the giant crapaud frog, fried and served with Creole sauce. Named 'mountain chicken' because of its taste. Now critically endangered, the dish lives on in cultural memory and with chicken substitutes.

lunch.name: Callaloo Soup
instructions: Boil soaked salted pigtail until tender, 30 min
Shred dasheen leaves, add to pot with coconut milk
Add okra, onion, garlic, thyme, whole Scotch bonnet (don't burst it unless you want extreme heat)
Simmer 25 min until dasheen leaves break down into thick green soup
Add crab pieces
Make small flour dumplings, drop into soup
Cook 10 more min
The soup should be thick, green, and rich with coconut
Remove Scotch bonnet before serving
lunch.description: Thick green soup of dasheen leaves, coconut milk, crab, and dumplings — Dominica's soul food. The salted pigtail gives deep umami, and the whole Scotch bonnet gives aroma without lethal heat (unless someone breaks it).

lunch.name: Provisions Plate (Boiled Ground Provisions)
instructions: Peel and chop root vegetables into large chunks
Boil in salted water until each is tender — dasheen takes longest, banana the least
Drain, arrange on plate
Serve with butter, flaked salt fish, sliced avocado
Drizzle coconut milk over the provisions
lunch.description: A plate of boiled root vegetables — dasheen, yam, green banana, breadfruit — with salt fish and avocado. The foundation of Dominican cooking, simple and sustaining.

lunch.name: Mountain Chicken (Crapaud Legs)
ingredients: 8 crapaud legs (giant ditch frog — Dominica's 'mountain chicken')
Seasoning: lime juice, garlic, thyme, green seasoning (cilantro, chive, celery, parsley, pepper)
Creole sauce: tomatoes, onion, garlic, Scotch bonnet, thyme
instructions: Note: crapaud is now critically endangered — this recipe documents a cultural tradition
Clean and season frog legs with lime juice, garlic, thyme, green seasoning
Marinate at least 1 hour
Dredge in seasoned flour
Fry until golden and crispy — the meat is white, tender, tastes like chicken
Make Creole sauce: sauté onion, garlic, add tomatoes, Scotch bonnet, thyme, simmer
Serve fried legs with Creole sauce, rice, and provisions (root vegetables)
Dominica is the only place this was a national dish — the name 'mountain chicken' refers to the taste and the fact that the frogs live in the mountains
lunch.description: Dominica's most famous and controversial dish — giant frog legs so meaty they're called 'mountain chicken.' Now critically endangered from chytrid fungus, this dish documents a culinary tradition that made Dominica unique. The 'why is it called chicken?' reveal went viral on food travel channels.

dinner.name: Creole Fish
ingredients: 4 fresh fish fillets or whole snapper
Seasoning: garlic, thyme, scallion, parsley, salt, black pepper
Creole sauce: 2 onions (sliced), 3 tomatoes, garlic, thyme, Scotch bonnet, green pepper, lime juice, oil
instructions: Clean fish, score sides if whole, marinate in lime, garlic, thyme, scallion, salt
Let sit at least 30 min
Dredge in flour, fry until golden and crispy on both sides
Make Creole sauce: sauté onions and garlic in oil until soft
Add sliced green pepper, tomatoes, thyme, Scotch bonnet
Cook until sauce is thick and fragrant
Pour sauce over fried fish
Squeeze fresh lime over everything
Serve with provisions (boiled root vegetables) or rice
dinner.description: Fried fish in spicy Creole tomato sauce — the way fish is eaten across Dominica. The fish is seasoned with local 'green seasoning' (herbs blended into a paste), fried crispy, then smothered in sauce.

imageCredit.author: Photo by Victor Monsour of Monsour's Photography

dinner.name: Titiwi Accras (Fish Fritters)
ingredients: 1 cup titiwi (tiny fish) or salt cod
instructions: Mix fish with batter ingredients
Drop spoonfuls in hot oil
Fry until golden and crispy
dinner.description: Crispy fritters made with tiny river fish.

dinner.name: Goat Water (Goat Stew)
instructions: Season goat with garlic, thyme, salt, pepper
Brown in oil
Add onion, cloves, bay leaf, Scotch bonnet
Add water to cover, bring to simmer
Cook low 60-90 min until goat is very tender
Add breadfruit if using
Make small flour dumplings, add to stew
Add a splash of rum
Simmer 15 more min
The stew should be thick, rich, and deeply flavored from the bones
dinner.description: Slow-cooked goat stew with dumplings — Dominica's answer to comfort food. The bones give the broth incredible body. The splash of rum near the end is the secret.

snacks.name: Cassava Farine
instructions: Grate cassava, squeeze out liquid
Toast in dry pan, stirring constantly
Add butter and salt
Cook until golden granules form
snacks.description: Toasted cassava granules — Dominica's traditional Kalinago food.

snacks.name: Accra and Floats
ingredients: Accra: salt cod (soaked, flaked), flour, baking powder, onion, garlic, Scotch bonnet, thyme, oil for frying
Floats: flour, baking powder, salt, sugar, butter, water, oil for frying
instructions: Accra: mix flaked salt cod with flour, baking powder, onion, garlic, Scotch bonnet, thyme into thick batter
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil, fry until golden
Floats: make simple dough, shape into rounds, fry until puffy and golden
Serve accra and floats together — the salty cod fritters and plain fried bread complement each other
snacks.description: Salt cod fritters paired with plain fried bread — Caribbean street food eaten in Dominica at any hour, especially Saturday mornings.

desserts.name: Banana Bread
instructions: Mash bananas, cream butter and sugar
Add eggs and vanilla
Fold in flour, baking soda, nutmeg
Bake at 175°C for 60 min
desserts.description: Moist banana bread with island nutmeg.

desserts.name: Coconut Fudge
instructions: Cook sugar and water to soft ball stage
Add grated coconut, lime zest, vanilla, salt
Stir constantly until mixture thickens and pulls from the sides of the pot
Pour onto greased tray
Score into squares while warm
Let cool and harden
Break into pieces
desserts.description: Dense coconut fudge — made with freshly grated coconut from the trees that grow everywhere. A simple sweet sold in paper bags at every village shop.

drinks.name: Sea Moss Drink
instructions: Soak sea moss overnight, wash
Boil until dissolved
Blend with milk, sugar, spices
Chill and serve

drinks.name: Rum Punch
instructions: Mix rum, lime, syrup, bitters
Serve over ice
Grate nutmeg on top
